open_points.subject: A07 operation-output disclosure
open_points.text: “a disclosure class only rises” and “lowers_class(any construct) -> never” conflict with “for an operation node, the class its binding declares for that output”; a binding can accept personal_data and declare an open output.
open_points.question: May an operation output have a lower disclosure class than the inputs supplied to that operation?
options: Allow the binding-declared output class even when it lowers the class
Require every operation output to be at least the highest class of the operation inputs
Treat an operation as an explicit declassification boundary requiring another authorization
open_points.default_guess: Require every operation output to be at least the highest class of the operation inputs.

open_points.subject: A07 agent-originated personal data
open_points.text: “no agent ever holds it” and “The owner ... is the only reader of personal data” conflict with rules allowing any agent to start a run with values whose flow-input port is personal_data and an authoring agent to add personal_data trial inputs or constants.
open_points.question: May an agent submit a clear personal_data value to the kernel, or must such requests be refused?
options: Allow agents to submit personal data but never return it
Refuse clear personal data supplied by an agent
Permit it only through service operation outputs
open_points.default_guess: Allow submission because the operative rule prohibits returning, not supplying, the value.

open_points.subject: A07 protected failure-detail length
open_points.text: “A failure_detail whose class is above open ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class” does not define what length measures.
open_points.question: Is the disclosed failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or characters after truncation?
options: UTF-8 byte length after truncation
Unicode scalar-value count after truncation
Original pre-truncation byte length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, truncated detail.

open_points.subject: A03 clock isolation
open_points.text: “every clock ... entry point” and State 0's “no clock” conflict with the closed trap list, which omits CPython 3.12 clock-bearing APIs such as time.clock_gettime, time.thread_time, os.times and resource.getrusage.
open_points.question: Are unlisted APIs that reveal time permitted, or must the sandbox prevent every clock-bearing API?
options: Only the enumerated entry points are forbidden
Every API exposing wall, monotonic, process or thread time is forbidden
Only wall-clock time is forbidden
open_points.default_guess: Forbid every clock-bearing API and make the release list exhaustive for CPython 3.12.

open_points.subject: A03 filesystem access
open_points.text: State 0 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”, while A03 permits opening paths in “the exchange directory and the read-only runtime”.
open_points.question: May user code directly read or write the exchange directory and read arbitrary runtime files?
options: Permit both locations exactly as A03 states
Hide both locations from user code and reserve them for the runner
Permit required runtime imports but deny explicit user file access
open_points.default_guess: Reserve the exchange directory for the runner and permit only runtime reads needed for imports.

open_points.subject: A03 sandbox-visible filesystem
open_points.text: “a read-only runtime” and “one private exchange directory” do not define the filesystem tree visible to code, its working directory, whether /proc or device files exist, or which runtime files are included.
open_points.question: What exact paths and virtual filesystems are visible inside the bubblewrap environment?
options: An empty root containing only the runtime and exchange directory
Also mount a minimal /proc and device set
Use a larger fixed runtime filesystem image
open_points.default_guess: Use an empty root with the fixed runtime, exchange directory, and only the minimum virtual files required by CPython.

open_points.subject: A03 resource accounting
open_points.text: “ResourceBounds ... are enforced ... with setrlimit (address space, processes)” does not say whether memory and process limits include the runner, apply per process or to the whole environment, or how child processes are counted.
open_points.question: What exactly is counted against memory_bytes and process_count?
options: Per-process address space and per-UID process count including the runner
Aggregate memory and all processes in the sandbox including the runner
Aggregate descendants while excluding the runner
open_points.default_guess: Count the runner and all descendants, with memory enforced as an aggregate sandbox limit.

open_points.subject: A03 caught resource-limit failures
open_points.text: “a limit hit ... resource_exhausted” requires detecting memory, process, scratch and output limit hits, but unlike trap hits no durable runner-to-parent signal is specified; code can catch MemoryError or a failed fork and return normally.
open_points.question: How is a resource-limit hit detected, and does it remain resource_exhausted when user code catches the resulting exception?
options: Any attempted limit breach is reported and wins even if caught
Only externally observed termination or excess is resource_exhausted
A caught limit exception may still succeed
open_points.default_guess: Record every attempted limit breach through a protected runner channel and classify it resource_exhausted even if caught.

open_points.subject: A03 scratch ceiling
open_points.text: The exchange directory is “bounded by sandbox_scratch_bytes_max”, but the text does not define whether the bound counts logical file sizes, allocated blocks, metadata, replaced files or simultaneously live bytes.
open_points.question: What usage measure triggers sandbox_scratch_bytes_max?
options: Sum of logical sizes of live files
Allocated filesystem blocks including metadata
Cumulative bytes written during the execution
open_points.default_guess: Use the sum of logical sizes of all live files in the exchange directory.

open_points.subject: A03 stdout and stderr
open_points.text: “Nothing the code prints ... is interpreted” and “never stdout” do not state how stdout and stderr are drained or bounded, although every execution is described as having bounded output.
open_points.question: What happens when function code writes an arbitrarily large amount to stdout or stderr?
options: Discard through a bounded nonblocking sink and continue
Count it against output_bytes
Treat excess diagnostic output as resource_exhausted
Allow the pipe to block until wall timeout
open_points.default_guess: Drain and discard through a fixed bounded sink without counting it as function output.

open_points.subject: A03 deterministic execution
open_points.text: The required test says “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice”, but the sandbox rules do not block other nondeterministic observations such as process identifiers, object addresses, resource usage and runtime filesystem metadata.
open_points.question: Is determinism a universal sandbox guarantee, and if so which remaining observable nondeterministic sources must be removed or trapped?
options: Guarantee determinism and close every observable source
Guarantee only the listed clock and randomness restrictions
Treat repeatability as a test expectation rather than an invariant
open_points.default_guess: Guarantee determinism and forbid or normalize every observable nondeterministic source.

open_points.subject: A03 audit-hook coverage
open_points.text: The runner “installs an audit hook that raises on socket, subprocess, ctypes” without naming the CPython audit events or operations included in those categories.
open_points.question: Which exact audit events and standard-library operations constitute a socket, subprocess or ctypes violation?
options: A release-pinned exhaustive event list
Any event whose name has a matching module prefix
A semantic deny-list implemented by wrappers as well as audit events
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-pinned exhaustive event list plus wrappers for operations that emit no adequate event.

open_points.subject: A16 token syntax
open_points.text: A token must be “at least 43 characters (32 bytes in base64url)”, but no base64url syntax or decoded-length check is required.
open_points.question: Must a token be valid base64url encoding of at least 32 bytes, or is any string of 43 characters accepted?
options: Validate base64url and decoded length
Accept any 43-character string
Measure at least 43 UTF-8 bytes without validating the alphabet
open_points.default_guess: Validate unpadded base64url and require at least 32 decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: A16 request-size accounting
open_points.text: Request size is “the bytes of the request message as received”, but the text does not identify whether that means the complete MCP frame, its JSON payload, a decoded operation object, or whether the token and transport envelope count.
open_points.question: Which exact byte sequence is measured against surface_request_bytes_max?
options: The complete serialized MCP message including token and envelope
Only the serialized operation arguments
The canonical JSON of the decoded request
open_points.default_guess: Count the complete serialized MCP request message received by the kernel.

open_points.subject: A16 configuration re-read
open_points.text: The kernel “reads the configuration file and compares the SHA-256 of its bytes ... when they differ ... it re-reads it”, but no rule says which file image governs the request if the file changes between those reads or while it is parsed.
open_points.question: Must hashing, parsing and installing the token list use one atomic snapshot of the configuration file?
options: Read and validate one opened-file snapshot
Hash once and parse a second read
Retry until two consecutive reads match
open_points.default_guess: Hash and parse the same bytes from one opened-file snapshot.

open_points.subject: A17 credential size
open_points.text: A credential file is decoded and used as an HTTP header, but neither A17 nor A20 places a size bound on the file or header value.
open_points.question: What happens when a credential file is arbitrarily large or exceeds the HTTP client's header limit?
options: Refuse it under bounded_text_bytes_max
Introduce a credential-specific release ceiling
Permit any size the HTTP dependency accepts
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a credential value above bounded_text_bytes_max during credential resolution.

open_points.subject: A17 credential text normalization
open_points.text: Credential content is decoded “without one trailing newline” and refused if it “holds ... a control character”, without defining newline form or the set of control characters.
open_points.question: Is one LF removed, is one CRLF removed as a unit, and which Unicode or ASCII code points count as control characters?
options: Remove one LF only and reject ASCII C0, DEL and remaining controls
Remove one LF or CRLF and reject Unicode control-category characters
Perform no newline removal and reject all controls
open_points.default_guess: Remove one terminal LF or CRLF and reject ASCII C0 and DEL characters in the remaining value.

open_points.subject: A17 secret-file race
open_points.text: The secret file is “read then” checked as a regular, owner-only file “without following a symbolic link”, but the text does not require the checks and content read to refer to the same opened file object.
open_points.question: How must the kernel prevent a path replacement between validation and reading the credential?
options: Open without following links and validate the opened descriptor before reading
Validate the path and then open it
Read twice and compare metadata
open_points.default_guess: Open once without following links, validate that descriptor, then read from it.

open_points.subject: A20 pinned dependencies
open_points.text: “A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of the sandbox runtime” gives only “CPython 3.12” and supplies neither the dependency set nor exact versions, including the bubblewrap requirement.
open_points.question: What exact dependency names and versions constitute release v1?
options: Provide a complete lock manifest including CPython patch version and bubblewrap
Pin only Python packages and CPython, treating bubblewrap as a host prerequisite
Leave exact versions to the build agent
open_points.default_guess: Provide a complete release lock manifest including CPython's patch version, all Python packages and bubblewrap.

open_points.subject: A20 oversized service responses
open_points.text: A20 says an over-ceiling response is “never a truncation”, while A09 says for 3xx, 4xx and 5xx responses “whatever the body's size — reading stops at the ceiling”.
open_points.question: When a non-2xx response body exceeds service_response_bytes_max, does the status-based outcome stand after truncating the body, or does response size determine a distinct failure?
options: Keep the status-based outcome and truncate only discarded diagnostic input
Treat every oversized response as the response-size failure
Read and discard the complete body without storing it
open_points.default_guess: Keep the status-based outcome and explicitly classify the bounded read as a diagnostic exception to the no-truncation rule.

open_points.subject: A20 release upgrades and admission
open_points.text: A release may change the pinned interpreter and dependencies, while AdmissionVerdict identity depends only on implementation and corpus; A04 reuses an existing verdict and activation without rerunning admission.
open_points.question: Does an admission verdict remain valid after upgrading to a release with a different sandbox runtime?
options: Reuse the verdict across releases
Include sandbox-runtime identity in the verdict and rerun admission
Keep the old runtime available for implementations admitted under it
open_points.default_guess: Include the sandbox-runtime identity in admission evidence and rerun admission after a runtime change.

open_points.subject: A21 completeness criterion
open_points.text: “complete security review” and “every_required_category” are asserted, but no authoritative category set, threat model, required analysis, or criterion for completeness is defined; the listed APPLICABLE entries merely reference decisions.
open_points.question: What makes the security review complete beyond containing these category labels and resolvable references?
options: Define a closed required-category set with threat, control and residual-risk fields
Treat the listed categories and references as sufficient by definition
Require an external security-review procedure or approval artifact
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed category set and require a threat, controlling decision and residual-risk outcome for each category.

open_points.subject: A21 authentication-token secrecy
open_points.text: The review marks “secrets” complete, but A17's no-store/no-log invariant protects service credentials, while owner and agent tokens are only prohibited from responses and from functions, flows and traces; their treatment in kernel logs, failure details and other store records is unstated.
open_points.question: Must authentication tokens be excluded from every log, failure detail, stored record and process argument just like service credentials?
options: Apply the full credential non-disclosure invariant to all tokens
Protect tokens only from responses, functions, flows and traces
Allow bounded diagnostic logging of token-derived data
open_points.default_guess: Apply the full service-credential non-disclosure invariant to owner and agent tokens.

open_points.subject: A13 non-executable-node ordering
open_points.text: The next executable node is the smallest ready node, and records for nodes that “become non-executable together” are ordered, but the text never defines when skip and upstream_failed propagation occurs relative to independent ready-node execution.
open_points.question: When an upstream conclusion simultaneously makes one node non-executable and another node ready, which record or execution happens first?
options: Propagate and record all skips/upstream failures before selecting another ready node
Select the smallest node_id across executable and newly non-executable nodes
Execute ready nodes first and propagate non-executable nodes only at quiescence
open_points.default_guess: Propagate all newly determined skip and upstream_failed conclusions before selecting the next executable node.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped aggregate outputs
open_points.text: Each mapped output list is measured only when delivered, and an oversized list fails the mapped node, but no order or atomicity rule says what happens when one output list is valid and another deliverable output list exceeds stored_value_bytes_max.
open_points.question: Are all mapped output lists validated atomically before any is delivered, or may earlier valid outputs remain delivered when a later output is oversized?
options: Validate all deliverable outputs first and deliver none if any fails
Process output ports in name order and keep earlier deliveries
Fail only dependants of the oversized output port
open_points.default_guess: Validate all deliverable aggregate outputs atomically and deliver none if any exceeds the ceiling.

open_points.subject: A13 request loss during advancement
open_points.text: A run advances “inside a request” until no node can execute, but no rule states what happens if the MCP client disconnects or cancels while that request is executing.
open_points.question: Does run advancement continue to quiescence after the initiating request is disconnected, or does it stop at a defined durable boundary?
options: Continue to quiescence and persist the result
Stop after the current node and leave the run running for recovery
Cancel the run
Abort only before any effect is sent
open_points.default_guess: Continue to quiescence because client disconnection is not an owner's cancel decision.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP operation set
open_points.text: State 0 K-11 says the fixed surface is “inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel”, while the State 0 action table and A16 additionally require capture, release, rollback, propose binding, compose/prove, and agent activation.
open_points.question: Which exact actions are distinct operations on the fixed MCP surface, and which are intended to be subforms of the names in K-11?
options: Every primary-action row is a distinct operation
Treat capture, rollback, proposal and composition as forms of author, but add release explicitly
Use only the literal K-11 list and remove the unmatched actions
open_points.default_guess: Expose every primary-action row as a distinct typed operation.

open_points.subject: approve-effect action result
open_points.text: State 0 says approving an effect outputs “the effect runs on the exact input shown”, while A10 says approval can succeed and then a pre-send check can fail, so “nothing is sent” and the approval stays unused.
open_points.question: Is approval itself successful when the approved effect cannot be sent, and what result must the approve request return?
options: Return success with the resulting operation_failed run state
Refuse the approval action and leave it requested
Record approval but return a distinct send failure
open_points.default_guess: Record the approval decision and return success together with the resulting operation_failed element and run state.

open_points.subject: declared idempotency key
open_points.text: State 0 says “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”, while A08 says “The key travels to the service as those input fields themselves” and “the kernel adds no header or field of its own”.
open_points.question: Does the kernel transmit a separately generated idempotency key, or only validate and hash already supplied input fields for its EffectAttempt record?
options: Transmit no additional key; only the declared input fields travel
Add the computed digest as an HTTP header
Add a generated key field to the request body or query
open_points.default_guess: Transmit no additional key and record only the digest of the declared input-field values.
